summary: Investigated and fixed an 'Invalid agent protocol response' error caused by the agent server leaking internal `linked` fields into registry status responses, and by Windows backslash paths not being normalized when deriving registry clone names (which also created a duplicate registration). Then, after clarifying the architecture, decided that every extension (Unity, Git, Svelte, Activity, Ask User) should live in the gizmo-registry as a Pi extension with an optional paired Gizmo web integration, and spawned four parallel subagents to migrate Unity, Git, Svelte, and Activity from the Gizmo source repo into gizmo-registry as isolated registry artifacts.
decisions: Registry status serialization must not leak the internal `linked: string[]` field on each registry entry — only the protocol-declared fields are emitted (name, url, optional commit, addedAt, extensions).
Registry clone names must normalize Windows backslashes before deriving the stem, so the same path produces the same name and prevents duplicate registrations.

Every extension is fundamentally a Pi extension; it may optionally include a paired Gizmo web integration. Gizmo must contain no extension-specific behavior (no Unity, Git, Svelte, Activity, or Ask User knowledge).

The target registry layout puts each extension under `extensions/<id>/` with `pi-extension.ts` and an optional `src/web/index.ts` exporting `gizmoWebExtension`, plus a generated sibling bundle like `extensions/unity.web.js`.

The existing `GizmoServerExtension` implementations are treated as transitional; their backend behavior moves into proper Pi extensions and the legacy host-extension system will be removed from Gizmo.
errors: 'Invalid agent protocol response' — root cause: agent server was emitting an undeclared `linked` field on each registry entry in the `registry.status` response, which the strict TypeBox protocol schema (with `additionalProperties: false`) rejected during `parseRegistryStatus`.
